newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Jardine Fleming suspends executive over PNG.
newsitem.headline: HK's Jardine Fleming suspends executive over PNG.

text.p: Hong Kong finance house Jardine Fleming said on Friday it has suspended an assistant director after his name came up in an inquiry in Papua New Guinea into a mercenary deal.
"Rupert McCowan, a Jardine Fleming employee, has been suspended on full pay in order to assist in the group's inquiries," Jardine Fleming spokesman David Dodwell said.
Dodwell said the company launched an internal inquiry two weeks ago when reports of its involvement surfaced at a government probe in Port Moresby, capital of the South Pacific nation.

Sacked PNG army chief Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok told the inquiry that McCowan attended a London meeting in September at which the mercenary deal was discussed. He also said McCowan acted as the financial adviser in the mercenary deal.

The mercenaries were hired by the PNG government headed by Prime Minister Julius Chan to help quell secessionist rebels in Bougainville, the site of a valuable copper mine. Chan has stepped aside while the PNG inquiry continues.

"(There are) an awful lot of inflammatory and inaccurate claims being made," Dodwell said. "We are taking extremely seriously any material claims that are being made. We have sought external legal counsel to investigate independently whether there are any claims to answer."
The company's independent inquiry will last for as long as necessary and at least until the PNG government inquiry ended, which would not be before May, he added.
"It is the present intention of the (Jardine Fleming) group to make no further public statements until its internal inquiry is complete," he said.
